answer.headline: Monthly anomalies in DEN departure cancellation rates cannot be established for September 2025–August 2026

claims.text: DEN departure cancellation rates by month were {F13} in September 2025, {F14} in October 2025, {F15} in November 2025, {F16} in December 2025, {F17} in January 2026, {F18} in February 2026, {F19} in March 2026, {F20} in April 2026, {F21} in May 2026, {F22} in June 2026, {F23} in July 2026, and {F24} in August 2026.

assumptions: DEN refers to Denver International Airport in Denver, CO, the airport returned by entity resolution.
Departure cancellation rate means the catalog metric cancel_rate, defined as cancelled divided by scheduled departures on on-time departure records.
A monthly anomaly means a month flagged by the catalog anomaly operator in time mode, which scores year-over-year changes with a robust z at the default threshold.
limitations: On-time departure coverage is September 2025 through August 2026. The prior year is out of coverage, so year-over-year anomalies cannot be established.
An empty flag list is not a positive finding that each month fell inside a normal range.
On-time records cover domestic flights of reporting carriers only, and exclude international flights and non-reporting carriers.
Causes of month-to-month differences are not identified. Terminal capacity, unmet demand, fares, and profitability are not measured here.
